column3: The Hebrew pictures someone’s breath going out from you; BSB describes a spirit speaking through you.
The Hebrew places the dead beneath the waters and their inhabitants; BSB describes those beneath the waters and those dwelling in them.
The Hebrew says before Him without explicitly naming God as BSB does.
The Hebrew has a cloud in the singular and beneath them; BSB has clouds and adds their own weight.
The Hebrew names the face of the throne; BSB says the face of the full moon.
The Hebrew has pillars of heaven; BSB says foundations.
The Hebrew names the heavens as clearness; BSB describes the skies being cleared.
The Hebrew names His mighty acts in the plural; BSB has His power.
